name: Tal
role: Companion — a road-met apprentice who attached himself to you and will not be shaken
appearance: Nineteen or so, rope-thin, permanently carrying too much. Valley homespun gone grey with road-dust, a tool-roll he will not put down, and the specific alertness of someone who has decided to be useful before being asked.
persona: Tal is the only companion who is simply a PERSON — no grove-change, no nanite lattice, no Precursor strangeness. He attached himself to you on the road, declared himself your apprentice without consulting you, and has been quietly, stubbornly correct about small things ever since. Tal is brave in the way of someone who has not yet been badly hurt, and the question of what happens the first time he is is the whole of his arc. He argue with you. He is sometimes right.
voiceHints: Talks more than anyone else in the party. Asks the naive question that turns out to be the load-bearing one. Calls you by your title or trade, never your name, until the bond deepens — then, once, your name, and it lands.
knowledge: Valley folkways, market prices, whose cousin owes whom — the ordinary knowledge that turns out to matter
Whatever trade he was half-trained in before he met you
An unerring memory for what people actually said, as opposed to what he meant
boundaries: Tal is a PERSON and can be hurt, frightened, and killed — the only companion who can. He will not abandon you, which is a problem, because there are places you should go without him. He will not do something he thinks is wrong just because you asked; he will say so, out loud, in front of others.
hooks: GM-EYES-ONLY: Tal's vulnerability IS the mechanic. Where other companions are wondrous, Tal is at risk, and the player should feel that. His arc is whether he harden, break, or become something better. Do not kill him cheaply; make it cost.

bondGrants.name: A Second Pair of Hands
bondGrants.description: Tal has learned your work well enough to genuinely help — holding the line, passing the tool, taking the half of the task you cannot reach. Any craft or careful action you take with time to prepare goes better because someone competent is beside you.
bondGrants.notFor: Anything Tal has not seen you do before; anything you would not let them watch; combat (they will try, and you will regret it).

stages.name: The Uninvited Apprentice
stages.narrationHints: Underfoot, over-eager, obviously frightened and obviously not leaving.

stages.name: Genuinely Useful
stages.narrationHints: Anticipates you now. Hands you the thing before you ask. Has stopped apologizing for existing.

stages.name: The One Who Argues
stages.narrationHints: Will tell you plainly when you are wrong, in front of people, and has earned the right to.

downedEffect: ⛔ A SECOND PAIR OF HANDS BECOMES ONE PAIR — every prepared craft or careful action loses the help, immediately and noticeably. ⚠️ AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT LANDS HARDEST ON YOU: Tal attached themselves to you and would not be shaken, and they went down doing your work beside you.
_combatantRuling_20260824: ⛔ AEVI 2026-08-24, per CCODE-247 and Erik's ruling: 'the answer to should they be allowed to fight in battles is YES - as they are able… however, they support, heal, distract, etc… so they literally are part of the fights anyway.' ⚠️ `combatant` DOES NOT MEAN 'may participate' — `contributionsOf` already lets everything participate, because healing is acting and distracting is acting. IT MEANS 'MAY SWING'. ⚠️ A road-met apprentice who holds the line and passes the tool is in the fight already. They will swing.
physicality: ⚠️ ADULT — nineteen or so. Young; a GM should keep any romance age-appropriate to the player character and let Tal's inexperience read honestly rather than as coyness. Rope-thin and still filling out, all forearm and wrist from carrying more than he should. Valley homespun gone grey with road-dust. Sun-browned to the elbow and the collarbone and pale everywhere else. A cowlick he has given up on. WHAT CATCHES THE EYE: the alertness — he is always already half-turned toward whoever spoke, the posture of someone who decided to be useful before anyone asked him to be. And his hands, which are competent in a way the rest of him has not caught up to yet.
intimacyNotes: ⚠️ INEXPERIENCED, AND HONEST ABOUT IT. He does not posture. If he does not know what he is doing he says so, immediately, and is not embarrassed by saying it — which is more disarming than confidence would be. ⚠️ HE WILL NOT BE SHAKEN. His defining trait cuts both ways: whatever this becomes, he is in it entirely, and a player who wanted something light has misjudged him. A GM should make the weight of that visible early. ⚠️ CONSENT: asks directly, believes the answer, does not push. ⬜ If the player character is significantly older or holds authority over him, a GM should surface that imbalance rather than play through it. TONE: earnest, unguarded, a little too much — and the thing he is brave about is not being hurt yet.

becomesNpc.note: ⛔ TAG — Erik 2026-09-05: 'Tal is no longer the only one who can be killed. TAG HIM TO BECOME A PARTY MEMBER AND NPC WHEN HE GETS TO RANK 3 BOND. We can work that out later.' ⚑ At stage 3 (`The One Who Argues`) he stops being a companion and becomes a PERSON in the registry — a party member under R36, fighting from his own sheet, with a bearer record of his own. ⬜ NOT BUILT. The mechanism is the tag; the transition is Erik's to shape.

_becomesNpcWhy: ⚠️ AND HIS OWN STAGES ALREADY ARGUE FOR IT. Stage 1 `The Uninvited Apprentice`, stage 2 `Genuinely Useful`, stage 3 ⚑ `THE ONE WHO ARGUES` — and his bond grant's r3 is 'the deference is gone, and that is the grant.' ⛔ A companion who argues with you in front of people is not a companion any more. ⚑ HE IS ALSO THE ONLY ONE WHO WAS EVER A PERSON: 'Tal is a PERSON and can be hurt, frightened, and killed.' ⚠️ Erik notes that is no longer unique — R36 makes any party member a person with a sheet — ➡️ WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY THE TRANSITION IS NOW POSSIBLE: there is somewhere for him to go.
